first_impression.reaction: OK, good, it actually tells me what it is in the first couple of lines and gives me three examples straight away. No pop-up, no life story. I'll keep going to see the ideas. The Key takeaways are a bit abstract though. I wanted the ideas themselves listed there, not advice about planning.

journey.quote: Instead of scanning a board for a name, each guest takes something, finds something or does something to learn where they sit: a card tied to a sweet, a glass of champagne with their name on it, a photo pinned to a wall.
journey.reaction: That's the answer, right up top. Exactly what I searched for.

journey.quote: Choose a style by what guests will do at it: take something, find something or do something.
journey.reaction: Fine as a framework, but on my phone I want the actual ideas in the summary so I can screenshot it and go. This makes me scroll to find them.

journey.section: Finish the Table Plan Before You Choose a Display
journey.quote: If you are new to it, here is [what Wonderland Studio does](https://weddedwonderland.com/expert-advice/what-is-wonderland-studio), alongside our other [wedding planning tools](https://weddedwonderland.com/wedding-planning-tools).
journey.reaction: This section is a pile of links to their own stuff before I've seen a single idea. I get the point, finish your plan first, but I skimmed past it fast.

journey.quote: Few things welcome a guest more warmly than a glass with their name on it.
journey.reaction: Cute, and I like that it also says to have non-alcoholic glasses. This is the bit I came for.

journey.quote: Pair it with a plain alphabetical list to one side so nobody has to hunt across continents for their name.
journey.reaction: Practical. This is the kind of tip that makes me think the writer has actually been to a wedding.

journey.section: A Screen or QR Lookup on Arrival
journey.quote: Never rely on a phone alone.
journey.reaction: Good, honest. I was going to do a QR code, now I'll keep a printed list too.

journey.quote: Queensland guidance for events is a sound reference here.
journey.reaction: Why Queensland? I'm not in Australia. Felt like a random government document dropped in, and it's a dense block on a phone. I skimmed it.

journey.quote: Alphabetical by surname is faster for guests to search, especially with a long list.
journey.reaction: Nice, short FAQ answers. Easy to scan.

unanswered_questions: Roughly what do these cost to do? Is a QR screen cheaper or dearer than a printed wall?
Is there a template or example I can actually use for the QR or screen version?
When was this written or updated? Is it still current in 2026?

turn_offs_found.quote: Choose a style by what guests will do at it: take something, find something or do something.
turn_offs_found.why: The summary doesn't list the ideas, so I have to scroll to get the actual answer.

turn_offs_found.quote: Build it in [Wonderland Studio](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-studio), our planning app for seating charts and RSVPs, so the list you send to the stationer or the screen is the same list your RSVPs produced.
turn_offs_found.why: A product plug and five links sitting between me and the ideas I searched for.

would_share_with: My fiance, for the map and champagne ideas
My sister, who is helping with the reception styling

cta_reaction.quote: If you are marrying overseas, our [Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=our-favourite-interactive-seating-charts&utm_content=secondary) service pairs you with one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as your single point of contact.
cta_reaction.why: I came for seating chart ideas, not a planner. I'm not marrying overseas, so this isn't for me. It's polite and not pushy, which I appreciate, but I'd bookmark the page rather than enquire.

top_3_changes: Put the actual ideas in the Key takeaways so a phone reader gets the answer without scrolling. OLD: "- Choose a style by what guests will do at it: take something, find something or do something." NEW: "- Choose a style by what guests will do at it: take something (a sweet, a named champagne glass, a tagged key), find something (a card wall, a map, a mirror) or do something (a screen or QR lookup)."

Trim the link stack before the ideas start. OLD: "Build it in [Wonderland Studio](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-studio), our planning app for seating charts and RSVPs, so the list you send to the stationer or the screen is the same list your RSVPs produced. If you are new to it, here is [what Wonderland Studio does](https://weddedwonderland.com/expert-advice/what-is-wonderland-studio), alongside our other [wedding planning tools](https://weddedwonderland.com/wedding-planning-tools)." NEW: "Build it in [Wonderland Studio](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-studio), our planning app for seating charts and RSVPs, so the list you send to the stationer or the screen is the same list your RSVPs produced."

Explain why an Australian state guide applies to a reader anywhere. OLD: "Queensland guidance for events is a sound reference here." NEW: "Wherever you marry, Queensland Government guidance on accessible events is a sound reference here."

No invented brand facts; cost and update-date gaps listed as unanswered questions, not filled in
Suggested edits use exact old/new strings and add no new facts, prices, fees, commissions, supplier sourcing or vetting claims
[[VERIFY]] markers and HTML comments treated as invisible

open_questions.question: Persona voice asks 'Is this still true in 2026?'. Should the post show a visible updated date? Out of scope for a copy edit, so it's raised here only.

assumptions: The search visitor is not planning an overseas wedding, so the Concierge CTA is not relevant to her. This follows from the persona card having no destination goal.
She reads on a phone, so how long sections are and how much she has to scroll before the ideas start count for more than they would on desktop.
